examples.en: Milk is a good source of calcium.
Sunlight is a source of vitamin D.

examples.ko: 이 공장이 도시에 전기를 보내는 공급원이에요.
examples.en: This plant is the source supplying electricity to the city.
Fish is good as a protein source.
The food supply was cut off, so people had a hard time.

examples.ko: 저는 새로운 단백질 공급원을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a new source of protein.

explain: '공급원'은 필요한 것을 내주는 곳이나 물건이에요. 영양이나 에너지 이야기에서는 '단백질 공급원', '에너지 공급원'처럼 자주 써요. 물건을 파는 사람이나 회사는 '공급자'나 '거래처'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Chicken is a good source of protein.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영양 이야기에서 '무엇의 공급원'이라고 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in nutrition talk: 'a source of something'.

phrases.en: Carbohydrates are the body's source of energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이나 기계에 힘을 주는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for whatever gives power to the body or a machine.

phrases.en: Fish is a major source of omega-3.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 공급원 중에서 가장 중요한 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out the most important one among several sources.

explain_en: '공급원' is a place or thing that provides what is needed. In nutrition and energy talk it is used as '단백질 공급원' or '에너지 공급원'. A person or company that sells goods is a '공급자' or '거래처'.

t90.ax: Milk is a good source of calcium.

examples.en: How do you make the future form in Korean?
Try changing this sentence into the future form.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 건물이 모두 미래형이라서 신기해요.
examples.en: All the buildings in this city look futuristic, which is amazing.
I went to a futuristic car exhibition.

examples.ko: 내일 일정을 말할 때 미래형을 써요.
examples.en: I use the future form when talking about tomorrow's plans.
This building really looks futuristic.

explain: 문법에서는 '-(으)ㄹ 거예요' 같은 미래를 나타내는 형태를 가리켜요. 한국어는 '내일 가요'처럼 현재형으로도 미래를 말해요. '미래형 도시'처럼 명사 앞에 붙으면 미래적인 모습을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 미래형 문장을 세 개 만들어 보세요.
phrases.en: Please make three future-tense sentences.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문법 수업에서 미래를 나타내는 문장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence expressing the future, used in grammar class.

phrases.en: I changed this sentence to the future tense.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙여 형태를 바꾼다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-으로' shows changing something into that form.

phrases.en: This place looks like a futuristic city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문법 말고 미래적인 모습을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a futuristic look, outside of grammar.

explain_en: In grammar, it refers to forms that express the future, such as '-(으)ㄹ 거예요'. Korean can also talk about the future with the present form, as in '내일 가요'. Before a noun, as in '미래형 도시', it refers to a futuristic look.

examples.ko: 개인 소유물은 각자 잘 챙겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please look after your personal belongings.

examples.ko: 이 책은 도서관 것이지 제 소유물이 아니에요.
examples.en: This book belongs to the library, not to me.

examples.ko: 사람을 자기 소유물처럼 대하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not treat people like your possessions.

examples.ko: 화재로 소유물을 모두 잃어버린 가족이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a family that lost all its belongings in a fire.
I wrote the bag and watch on the list of belongings.
Legally, that land is the company's property.

explain: 안내문과 법률에서 '개인 소유물을 잘 챙기세요'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '내 물건'이나 '내 거'라고 해요. 사람을 '소유물'처럼 대한다고 하면 물건 취급한다는 비판이 돼요.

phrases.example: 아이를 부모의 소유물로 여기면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not regard a child as a parent's possession.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 물건처럼 대한다는 비판의 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used critically for treating a person like an object.

phrases.en: Please write your name on your personal belongings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 규칙에서 자주 보는 격식 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase often seen in notices and rules.

phrases.en: Please store your belongings in a locker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시설 안내문에서 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in facility notices.

explain_en: Signs and legal texts use it, as in 개인 소유물을 잘 챙기세요. In daily talk people say 내 물건 or 내 거. Saying someone treats a person like a 소유물 is a criticism of treating them like an object.

examples.en: I had the wedding ring made of pure gold.
Pure gold is soft, so it bends easily.
I gave a pure gold ring for the baby's first birthday.
This necklace is real pure gold, so it's expensive.
I went to the jewelry shop to sell pure gold.
Grandmother passed down a pure gold bracelet to me.

explain: '순금'은 다른 금속이 섞이지 않은 금이에요. 한국에서는 아기 돌잔치나 결혼 때 '순금 반지'를 선물하는 문화가 있어요. 다른 금속이 섞인 금은 '합금'이나 '14K'처럼 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: My grandmother gave me a pure gold ring as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서 선물로 자주 하는 물건이라 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, since it is a popular gift in Korea.

phrases.en: This necklace is made of pure gold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 말할 때 '-으로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-으로' to say what something is made of.

phrases.en: Pure gold necklaces are expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순금으로 된 장신구를 말할 때 '순금' 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the item name after 순금 to talk about jewelry made of it.

explain_en: '순금' is gold with no other metal mixed in. In Korea there is a custom of giving a '순금 반지' for a baby's first birthday or a wedding. Gold mixed with other metals is called '합금' or labeled like '14K'.

examples.en: A rule like that these days is out of step with the times.

examples.ko: 사극에서 휴대폰이 나오면 시대착오라는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: If a cell phone appears in a historical drama, people call it an anachronism.

examples.ko: 아직도 그런 말을 하다니 시대착오 아닌가요?
examples.en: Isn't it out of touch to still say things like that?
His way of thinking is close to being outdated.

examples.ko: 영화에 시대착오가 한 군데 있어서 웃음이 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was one anachronism in the movie, and it made me laugh.

examples.ko: 시대착오를 피하려고 역사 자료를 꼼꼼히 확인했어요.
examples.en: To avoid anachronisms, I checked the historical sources carefully.

explain: 시대에 뒤떨어진 생각이나 행동을 비판할 때 써요. 또 작품 속 배경과 맞지 않는 물건이나 말이 나오는 것도 시대착오라고 해요. 형용사처럼 쓰고 싶을 때는 '시대착오적'을 써요.

phrases.en: That system is criticized as anachronistic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡은 생각이나 제도를 비판하는 말을 인용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to quote criticism of an outdated idea or system.

phrases.en: That period drama stirred an anachronism controversy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품 배경과 맞지 않는 물건이나 말이 나왔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an item or word doesn't fit the setting of a work.

phrases.en: Viewers pointed out the film's anachronism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품 속 시대에 맞지 않는 부분을 찾아 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when noting a part that doesn't fit the era in a work.

explain_en: Use it to criticize thoughts or actions that are out of date. It also names the mistake when an object or phrase in a story doesn't fit its setting in time. To use it like an adjective, say '시대착오적'.

examples.en: It's all in the past now, so let's forget it.
Grandmother sometimes smiles as she remembers the old days.
That kind of hardship has already become a thing of the past.
Please don't keep bringing up the past.

examples.ko: 동창들을 만나면 옛일 이야기로 밤을 새워요.
examples.en: When we meet our old classmates, we stay up all night talking about old times.
Our fight is already ancient history.

explain: '과거'보다 정감 있고 '지금은 지나간 일'이라는 느낌이 강해요. '옛일이 되다', '옛일을 떠올리다'처럼 자주 써요. '옛날 일'이라고 띄어 말해도 비슷해요.

phrases.en: That problem has now become a thing of the past.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금은 끝나서 지나간 일이 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something has ended and become part of the past.
phrases.en_equiv: to become a thing of the past

phrases.en: Grandfather told me about the old days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래전에 있었던 일을 말해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when telling about things that happened long ago.

phrases.example: 그건 옛날 일이라서 잘 기억이 안 나요.
phrases.en: That was long ago, so I don't remember it well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '옛일'을 띄어서 말한 형태로, 뜻은 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out version of 옛일, with almost the same meaning.

explain_en: It feels warmer than '과거' and strongly suggests something that has passed. It is common in '옛일이 되다' and '옛일을 떠올리다'. Saying it as two words, '옛날 일', is nearly the same.

t90.ax: Our fight is already ancient history.

examples.ko: 이 산길은 외길이라서 길을 잃을 걱정이 없어요.
examples.en: This mountain trail is a single path, so there's no worry about getting lost.

examples.ko: 좁은 외길에서 차를 만나서 한참 뒤로 갔어요.
examples.en: I met a car on the narrow single-lane road and had to back up a long way.

examples.ko: 그분은 평생 한 분야의 외길을 걸어왔어요.
examples.en: He has walked a single path in one field his whole life.
There is only one road to the village.

examples.ko: 그 도자기 장인은 외길 인생을 살았어요.
examples.en: That pottery master lived a life devoted to one path.
It snowed and the single road froze over.

explain: 갈래가 없는 길이라서 '갈림길'과 반대예요. 길 이야기 말고도 한 분야만 계속 가는 삶을 말할 때 '외길 인생'이라고 해요. 이때는 '걷다'와 자주 어울려요.

phrases.en: He spent 30 years devoted solely to pottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일만 오래 해 온 사람을 칭찬하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It praises someone who has stuck with one kind of work for a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: to devote oneself to one path

explain_en: It is a road with no branches, so it is the opposite of '갈림길' (fork). Besides roads, people use '외길 인생' for a life spent on one field only. In that sense it goes well with the verb '걷다'.

examples.ko: 이때껏 한 번도 지각한 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I've never been late even once until now.
I've waited until now, but there's still no word.

examples.ko: 이때껏 모은 돈으로 작은 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened a small shop with the money I've saved so far.
I didn't know that fact until now.
I've held back well until now, but this is my limit.
Where have you been all this time without any word?

explain: '지금까지'와 같은 뜻인데 조금 예스럽고 글 같은 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '여태껏'도 있어요. 과거부터 지금까지 이어진 일에 쓰고, 뒤에 '없다', '몰랐다'처럼 부정하는 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: I didn't know that fact until now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 이때껏보다 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but used more often in speech than 이때껏.

phrases.en: I haven't done my homework until now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 쉽고 일반적인 말이라 어디서나 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common, neutral way; natural anywhere.

phrases.example: 이때껏 그 가게가 여기 있는 줄 몰랐어요.
phrases.en: I never knew that shop was here until now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 부정하는 말이 붙어 '지금에야 알았다'는 놀라움을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With a negative, it conveys surprise at only now finding out.

explain_en: It means the same as '지금까지' (until now) but sounds a little old-fashioned or bookish. A similar word is '여태껏'. It is used for things continuing from the past up to now, and is often followed by negatives like '없다' or '몰랐다'.

examples.ko: 불이 나면 탈출구로 빨리 나가야 해요.
examples.en: If there's a fire, you must get out quickly through the exit.
At the theater I first checked where the exit was.

examples.ko: 요즘 너무 힘들어서 어디론가 탈출구를 찾고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm so worn out these days that I want to find a way out somewhere.
The exit was blocked, and people panicked.

examples.ko: 이 게임에서는 탈출구를 찾는 게 목표예요.
examples.en: The goal in this game is to find the way out.
Every building has exit signs.

explain: 위험하거나 갇힌 곳에서 빠져나가는 길이에요. 건물의 초록색 표지는 보통 '비상구'라고 부르고, '탈출구'는 더 넓게 쓰여요. 힘든 상황에서 벗어날 방법을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The emergency exit is at the end of that hallway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물의 초록색 표지가 있는 출구는 보통 '비상구'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The green-signed exit in a building is usually called '비상구'.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a way out of this hard situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길뿐 아니라 어려움에서 벗어날 방법을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a way out of difficulty, not only a physical path.
phrases.en_equiv: to look for a way out

phrases.en: There is no way out of this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠져나갈 길이 전혀 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say there is no way to get out at all.

explain_en: It is the way out of a dangerous or trapped place. The green sign in buildings is usually called '비상구', while '탈출구' is used more broadly. It can also mean a way to escape a hard situation.

examples.en: Don't fidget with your fingers during class.

examples.ko: 아기가 잠에서 깨려는지 이불 속에서 꼼지락거려요.
examples.en: The baby seems to be waking up and is wriggling under the blanket.
It was cold, so I waited for the bus wiggling my toes.

examples.ko: 방에서 혼자 뭘 그렇게 꼼지락거리고 있어요?
examples.en: What are you fiddling with all by yourself in your room?

examples.ko: 손을 꼼지락거리는 걸 보니 긴장했나 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you fidget with your hands, you must be nervous.
I dawdled in the morning and was late for school.

explain: '꼼지락거리지 말고 빨리 해'처럼 굼뜬 사람을 재촉할 때 자주 들어요. 손가락이나 발가락을 조금씩 움직이는 것 외에, 작은 일을 느릿느릿 만지작거리는 것도 가리켜요. 벌레나 작은 동물이 기어가는 느낌은 '꼬물거리다'가 더 잘 어울려요. '꼼지락대다'로 바꿔 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: The child is wiggling his feet under the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼼지락거리다'와 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 꼼지락거리다, so they are interchangeable.

phrases.en: The baby is wiggling its fingers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 부사를 써서 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, used with another verb to show the movement.

phrases.en: I dawdled in the morning and was late for school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굼뜨게 시간을 보내다 늦는 상황에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when dawdling makes you late.

explain_en: You often hear it when someone is told to hurry, as in '꼼지락거리지 말고 빨리 해'. Besides moving fingers or toes a little at a time, it also covers fiddling slowly with small tasks. For a bug or small animal crawling, '꼬물거리다' fits better. You can swap in '꼼지락대다' too.

t90.ax: Don't fidget with your fingers during class.

examples.en: He always fiddles with his phone when he's nervous.
The child is playing while fiddling with a doll.
I just kept fingering my handkerchief in the interview waiting room.
Why do you keep fiddling with your hair?
I was fiddling with a coin and dropped it on the floor.

examples.ko: 수업 중에 펜을 만지작대지 말고 집중하세요.
examples.en: Don't fiddle with your pen during class; focus.

explain: 손으로 자꾸 이리저리 만지는 모습이에요. 긴장하거나 심심하거나 고민할 때 무의식적으로 하는 행동에 잘 어울려요. 같은 뜻으로 '만지작거리다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He is fiddling with a pen.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만지작대다'와 같은 뜻으로 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 만지작대다, and used more often.

phrases.en: He thought for a long time while fiddling with his keys.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 행동과 같이 일어나는 것을 말할 때 '-면서'로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with -면서 to show it happens alongside another action.

phrases.en: Please don't keep fiddling with it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자꾸 만지는 행동을 말릴 때 쓰는 부탁이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request used to stop someone from touching something repeatedly.

explain_en: It describes touching something over and over with your hands. It suits actions done unconsciously when nervous, bored or worried. '만지작거리다' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

t90.ax: Why do you keep fiddling with your hair?

examples.en: The bear lumbered off into the forest.
The child came waddling out.
My knee hurt, so I climbed the stairs stiffly.
The man came shambling toward the door.
The penguin waddles across the ice.
Stop dawdling along and come quickly!

explain: '걷다', '걸어가다', '올라가다' 같은 움직임 말 앞에서 주로 써요. 큰 몸이나 불편한 다리로 천천히 걷는 모습을 그릴 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: Grandfather walked with slow, stiff steps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 짝말로, 몸이 무겁거나 불편해서 천천히 걷는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, showing slow walking because the body is heavy or sore.

phrases.en: I climbed the mountain with heavy steps like a bear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 천천히 올라가는 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits slowly and laboriously climbing up.

phrases.en: He shuffled out with a sleepy face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 느리고 둔한 걸음으로 어디에서 나오는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes coming out of somewhere with slow, clumsy steps.

explain_en: It is mostly used before movement verbs like '걷다', '걸어가다' and '올라가다'. It fits scenes of a big body or sore legs moving slowly.

examples.en: While traveling, I experienced a rediscovery of myself.

examples.ko: 이 책의 주제는 한국 음식의 재발견이에요.
examples.en: The theme of this book is the rediscovery of Korean food.

examples.ko: 옛 노래의 재발견 덕분에 다시 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the rediscovery of the old song, it became popular again.
Travel was a kind of rediscovery for me.
The rediscovery of traditional markets is a hot topic.
Rediscovery needs a fresh point of view.

explain: 처음 찾아내는 '발견'과 달리 이미 알고 있던 것의 가치를 새롭게 깨닫는 것을 말해요. 책 제목이나 기사 제목에 '~의 재발견'이라는 형태로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This trip was a chance for rediscovery for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재발견'에 '의'를 붙여 새롭게 깨닫는 계기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 의 to 재발견 describes an occasion that lets you see something anew.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 오래된 노래가 요즘 재발견되고 있어요.
phrases.en: That singer's old songs are being rediscovered these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 하는 일이 아니라 어떤 것의 가치가 다시 알려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the value of something becomes known again, rather than someone doing the rediscovering.

phrases.en: The title of this article is 'The Rediscovery of Traditional Markets.'
phrases.nuance_ko: '~의 재발견' 형태로 제목에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '~의 재발견' pattern is common in titles.

explain_en: Unlike '발견' (finding something for the first time), it means realizing anew the value of something you already knew. It shows up often in book and article titles in the form '~의 재발견'.

en: with a poke; with a jab; with a tap

examples.en: My friend poked me on the shoulder.

examples.ko: 화면에서 원하는 사진을 콕 눌러 보세요.
examples.en: Tap the photo you want on the screen.

examples.ko: 이 지도에서 우리 집 위치를 콕 짚어 줄게요.
examples.en: I will point out exactly where our house is on this map.
The baby poked the balloon with a finger.
The bird pecked at the berry and ate it.

examples.ko: 그 말이 제 마음에 콕 박혔어요.
examples.en: Those words stuck in my heart.

explain: 콕은 작고 뾰족한 것으로 한 번 찌르거나 누르는 소리와 모양을 흉내 낸 말이에요. '콕 집어서 말하다'는 여러 가운데 하나를 정확히 말할 때 자주 써요. 집에만 머무는 것을 '집콕'이라고 하는 말도 있어요.

phrases.example: 문제가 뭔지 콕 집어서 말해 줄래요?
phrases.en: to point out exactly
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가운데 하나를 정확히 가리켜 말한다는 뜻으로 써요. 보통 '콕 집어서 말하다'로 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you single out exactly one thing among many. It usually appears as 콕 집어서 말하다.

explain_en: 콕 imitates the look and sound of a small, sharp poke or press. 콕 집어서 말하다 is a common way to say pointing out one exact thing among many. There is also the slang 집콕, meaning staying home all the time.

t90.ax: Those words stuck in my heart.
